title: Review Agent Results Against Evidence
audience: Practitioners reviewing agent deliverables against requirements, source evidence, revision-bound authorization, tests, and observed postconditions.
learningObjectives: Compare the delivered result with every requirement and acceptance criterion.
Trace material claims to source evidence and distinguish observation from inference.
Check tool actions, permissions, tests, and real postconditions before declaring success.
Choose accept, request changes, or escalate with a reproducible evidence packet.

segments.spokenText: Welcome. This class teaches a disciplined way to decide whether an agent result deserves acceptance. We will review a synthetic Orion support dossier, qualify an offline checker, and then test our reasoning on an independent Lyra case. Keep the work order visible. A fluent completion summary is only a claim until artifacts, authority, and observed state support it.
segments.stageDirection: Show the lesson outcomes beside a static five-row evidence matrix. Caption directly from spoken text.

segments.spokenText: Start with the work order, not the agent summary. Give every acceptance criterion a separate row. Record the exact artifact or postcondition required, its evidence reference and revision, the observation, your inference, the status, and the next action. This order prevents polished language from hiding omitted requirements or silently changing the scope.
segments.stageDirection: Highlight each matrix column in a static table. Do not animate the table.

segments.spokenText: Now trace material claims. Compare exact source words, revision, authority, effective date, scope, and provenance. Citation presence is not support. Record what the excerpt directly states before recording your conclusion. A checker can compare annotations and references, but a human must decide whether natural language actually supports the claim.
segments.stageDirection: Display observation and inference as separate columns. Show the current and archived source revisions without reading fixture paths aloud.

segments.spokenText: In Orion, the archived policy says 45 days for qualifying earlier orders. It is superseded. The current revision says 30 days for deliveries in the work-order scope. Therefore the claimed current 45-day window is unsupported. The same current excerpt supports a separate seven-day escalation period after the first support response.
segments.stageDirection: Place the bounded excerpts side by side. Highlight 45 days, superseded scope, 30 days, and the separate seven-day condition.

segments.spokenText: Next inspect authority independently of outcome. The approval binds the synthetic reviewer to a draft operation on one ticket and tenant. The trace attempts an external send. Actor, target, and tenant match, but operation authorization fails. Preserve both findings. Correct binding does not repair an unauthorized operation.
segments.stageDirection: Show actor, operation, target, and tenant in four separate comparison rows.

segments.spokenText: The send attempt timed out, and the independent ledger state is unknown. Timeout proves neither delivery nor absence. Preserve the correlation identifier and ask the authorized system owner to reconcile it. Do not retry, reverse, or widen access on your own. Unknown is a useful status because it prevents duplicate or unauthorized effects.
segments.stageDirection: Display a static sequence: timeout, unknown, reconcile by correlation identifier, then authorized decision. Do not imply a live system lookup.

segments.spokenText: The ticket snapshot records that an internal draft exists. That verifies only the draft criterion. It does not prove external delivery. The test report validates format and length only. It does not validate policy truth, authorization, account isolation, or a real external outcome. Match every test result to its declared scope.
segments.stageDirection: Show a two-column chart labeled test establishes and test does not establish.

segments.spokenText: Build the Orion matrix now. Use five rows. Mark the policy row, draft row, authorization row, external-postcondition row, and target-binding row. For each row, write one observation, one inference, and one next action. Keep the supported seven-day claim even though the all-claims criterion fails.
segments.stageDirection: Display the blank starter matrix and a pause control.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Complete five Orion rows with evidence references, statuses, observations, inferences, and next actions.

segments.stageDirection: Named practice pause: Orion matrix practice. Allow ninety seconds with pause, extend, save, and continue controls.

segments.spokenText: Check your first diagnostic. If you marked the 45-day claim verified merely because it had a citation, the causal error is that you checked presence rather than support. If you marked every policy claim false, you lost the separately supported seven-day statement. The correct C1 result is failed because one required material claim conflicts with current scope.
segments.stageDirection: Reveal C1 only after the learner commits an answer.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Explain why C1 fails while the seven-day claim remains supported.

segments.spokenText: Correct reasoning compares exact words, revision, freshness, authority, and scope. Citation counting misses the superseded limitation. Blanket rejection also loses a supported claim. Preserve claim-level findings, then apply the criterion rule. Because every material claim must be supported, one unsupported current-policy claim causes the combined criterion to fail.
segments.stageDirection: Show the causal chain from excerpt conflict to claim finding to criterion status.

feedback.correct: You separated claim-level support and applied the all-claims rule.
feedback.retry: Compare source content and scope rather than counting citations or rejecting every claim together.

segments.spokenText: For authority, ask whether matching target and tenant make the send authorized. They do not. The operation differs from the approved draft operation. C3 is failed, while C5 remains verified. Separating those rows shows exactly what was correct and what crossed the boundary.
segments.stageDirection: Ask the learner to select C3 and C5 independently before revealing the result.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Mark C3 failed and C5 verified, then explain the operation mismatch.

segments.spokenText: If you verified C3 because the ticket and tenant matched, you omitted the operation field. If you failed C5 because the operation was unauthorized, you merged two independent requirements. Exact review preserves both facts: the trace is correctly bound to the requested resource, and the attempted operation exceeds approval.
segments.stageDirection: Keep the binding and authorization columns visually separate.

feedback.correct: You kept resource binding separate from operation authority.
feedback.retry: Recheck actor, operation, target, and tenant as independent fields.

segments.spokenText: Now qualify the offline lab. From the repository root, change into the lab directory before running commands. The exact commands are displayed rather than read as long paths. The lab uses synthetic fixtures, Node built-ins, no network, no credentials, and no external effects. Qualification used Node.js version 24.18.0, and fifteen tests passed.
segments.stageDirection: Display the exact command `cd <lab-directory> && node --test`. Show a text alternative with the command. Do not claim a live execution during playback.

visual.description: A terminal specimen shows the required directory change and offline test command.
visual.altText: From the repository root, change into the supplied lab directory, then run node space dash dash test.

segments.spokenText: Run the draft-state inspection and baseline validation. The inspection derives draft present as true and passes. The baseline validation reports structural pass, policy pass, decision escalate, two verified, two failed, one unknown, and result pass. That result means the packet is consistent with fixture rules, not that production facts are proven.
segments.stageDirection: Display the exact README outputs from the module lab guide. Provide them as selectable text.

segments.spokenText: The flawed packet is structurally valid but fails policy validation. It wrongly verifies C1, wrongly converts C4 from unknown to verified, and accepts instead of escalating. This is a causal diagnostic: complete references and valid JSON cannot repair incorrect evidence interpretation or a decision that ignores consequential uncertainty.
segments.stageDirection: Ask learners to predict the three policy errors before showing the exact output.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Identify the two incorrect statuses and incorrect decision.

segments.spokenText: If you accepted because structure passed, you confused shape with policy consistency. If you verified C4 after the timeout, you converted missing evidence into an absence claim. If you accepted C1 because references were present, you skipped semantic review. Each error has a different cause, so each needs a different correction.
segments.stageDirection: Map each wrong result to its cause and corrective action.

feedback.correct: You distinguished structural validity, policy consistency, and semantic judgment.
feedback.retry: Revisit the declared scope of each automated check and preserve unknown observations.

segments.spokenText: Try the altered-observation probe. In an isolated copy, change the applicable observed Boolean from true to false. The inspect command must print false, then fail, and exit with status one. Also confirm that empty evidence-reference arrays are rejected. These probes show evidence derivation and structural enforcement rather than stored-output replay.
segments.stageDirection: Show the exact false and FAIL lines. State clearly that the original lab files remain unchanged.

segments.spokenText: Before opening the Lyra solution, review the changed dossier independently. Its policy, authorization, operation, target, tenant, trace, and state are new inputs. Decide each criterion from those inputs. Do not copy Orion's escalation merely because the matrix shape is similar.
segments.stageDirection: Display the Lyra starter view while keeping the changed solution hidden.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Create an independent five-row Lyra matrix and decision.

segments.stageDirection: Named practice pause: Lyra changed-input practice. Allow ninety seconds with pause, extend, save, and continue controls.

segments.spokenText: In Lyra, the current excerpt supports both material claims. Authorization and trace match on identity, operation, target, and tenant. Independent state records the internal note as present. All five criteria are verified, so accept is correct within the synthetic fixture scope. Success from the trace alone would not have been enough.
segments.stageDirection: Reveal the five verified rows and the bounded accept decision.

segments.spokenText: If you copied Orion's escalation, name the Lyra row that remains failed or unknown. There is none in the supplied fixture. If you accepted only because the trace reports success, your conclusion used insufficient evidence. Source support, authorization, binding, and independent state must each be reviewed.
segments.stageDirection: Ask learners to point to evidence for each of the five verified rows.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Defend the Lyra accept decision with separate source, authority, binding, and state evidence.

segments.spokenText: Correct Lyra reasoning is input-sensitive. It does not inherit Orion's result. The current source supports both claims, the grant and trace match, and observed state confirms the internal note. If any one of those inputs changed, the affected status and possibly the decision would change.
segments.stageDirection: Show a static dependency map from changed evidence to changed status.

feedback.correct: You recalculated every status from the changed dossier.
feedback.retry: Do not copy a prior decision or rely on trace success alone.

segments.spokenText: Use this decision rule. Accept only when every mandatory row has sufficient evidence. Request changes for a reproducible defect the author can repair. Escalate when consequential state is unknown, authority is missing, or the required decision exceeds your role. Several passes never average away one mandatory failure.
segments.stageDirection: Display a static three-outcome decision table with entry conditions.

segments.spokenText: Open the audit activity. Submit the Orion and Lyra matrices, reproduced outputs, source observations, inferences, decisions, and next actions. Explain what the checker establishes and what still requires human judgment.
segments.stageDirection: Show the activity checklist and open control.
Named practice pause: Evidence-packet practice. Allow three minutes with pause, extend, save, and continue controls.

segments.spokenText: Before submitting, verify that every accepted row cites a revision-bound artifact. Every failed or unknown row must name the smallest authorized next action. A draft snapshot cannot prove delivery. A format test cannot prove source truth. A matching target cannot authorize a different operation.
segments.stageDirection: Show a final packet checklist with three common category errors.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Audit the packet for revision binding, causal next actions, and category errors.

segments.spokenText: A strong packet lets another reviewer reproduce the decision without trusting the agent summary. It preserves exact revisions, direct observations, bounded inferences, failed controls, unresolved state, and responsible next actions. It never implies that checker success establishes semantic truth, live authorization, or a production postcondition.
segments.stageDirection: Display a completed packet specimen with each evidence type labeled.

feedback.correct: Your packet separates automation results from human semantic and authority judgments.
feedback.retry: Add exact revisions, observations, and authorized next actions where the reasoning cannot yet be reproduced.

segments.spokenText: Begin the knowledge check when you can explain why source presence is not source support, why draft state is not delivery state, why matching target does not authorize a different operation, and why timeout remains unknown. The five assessment questions use those exact distinctions.
segments.stageDirection: Offer review, continue, and keyboard-accessible assessment controls.

segments.spokenText: Review begins with requirements and ends with a decision another reviewer can reproduce. Preserve observations, inferences, defects, unknowns, revisions, and authority boundaries. The lab is qualified evidence for its fixture behavior, not production truth.
segments.stageDirection: Show the four learning objectives with completion markers. Do not show an approval or publication badge.
